sections.title: Education, Culture and Technology
sections.description: This course takes an interdisciplinary approach to understanding the impact of technology and innovation on our society through anthropology, biology, STS, and economics. Beginning with early tool use and moving through scientific and medical advances, we conclude by examining today’s networked communities and the prevalence of personal devices and robotics, with a particular emphasis on its impact on education broadly understood. At its heart, the course explores how information and technology shape formal and informal education, affecting how humans relate to ourselves, each other, and the environment. We will analyze historical and contemporary conditions that shape techno-cultural relationships, such as agriculture, industry, disease, climate, education, and media. Through diverse readings and local field trips, students will gain insight into technology’s impact on human development, culture, and knowledge.
